newsitem.title: UK: BBH ad agency aims to rejuvenate Cointreau image.
newsitem.headline: BBH ad agency aims to rejuvenate Cointreau image.

text.p: Cointreau liqueur hopes to use a new, global advertising campaign to shake off an old-fashioned image and regain market share amid hot competition, Bartle Bogle Hegarty, the UK ad agency, said.

Cointreau, one of the top brands owned by Remy-Cointreau , the French drinks group, awarded its 8.0-million-pound ($12 million) account to BBH on Friday, its first big advertising campaign in about eight years.
"It's a pretty competitive market," Chris Harris, BBH's group director, said, referring to liqueurs.
"It's very challenging in all ways, because everyone is fighting to claim a share of (the consumer's) stomach," he told Reuters.
BBH, which won the campaign following a pitch to Cointreau by five agencies between July and September, said it would help reinvigorate the Cointreau brand and "make it younger".

The other agencies that pitched for the account were Abbott Mead Vickers and Howell Henry Chaldecott Lury in Britain, and the French agencies DDB Paris and FCB Paris. FCB Paris had previously held the account.
Euromonitor, the market analyst group, said in a recent study the global spirits market was expected to stagnate until the year 2000, mostly due to consumers choosing to drink less alcohol.

It also said high taxes, strict drink-driving laws and a decline of the "traditional family grouping with its associated spirits drinking" were forecast to lead to an 11 percent fall in real terms of France's spirits market.
BBH said it won the account by producing a "strategic presentation" for Cointreau that analysed its market, rather than the more usual ad agency approach of presenting creative work for pitches.
